sources.title: Attachment, Exploration, and Separation: Illustrated by the Behavior of One-Year-Olds in a Strange Situation
sources.authors: Ainsworth, M. D. S., & Bell, S. M.
sources.key_findings: Introduced the 8-episode, 3-minute-per-episode Strange Situation laboratory procedure with 56 one-year-old infants at Johns Hopkins, demonstrating how caregivers serve as a secure base for exploration and how reunion behavior distinguishes attachment organization.

sources.title: Biobehavioral Organization in Securely and Insecurely Attached Infants
sources.key_findings: Measured telemetric heart rate and salivary cortisol (15 and 30 minutes post-procedure) in 41 twelve-month-old infants during the Strange Situation, proving that insecure-avoidant infants show marked heart-rate elevation and adrenocortical cortisol increases despite minimal outward crying during separation and reunion.

sources.title: Maternal Buffering of Human Amygdala-Prefrontal Circuitry During Childhood but Not During Adolescence
sources.authors: Gee, D. G., Gabard-Durnam, L., Telzer, E. H., et al., & Tottenham, N.
sources.key_findings: Demonstrated via fMRI that maternal stimuli dampen childhood amygdala reactivity and induce mature-like negative regulatory connectivity between the medial prefrontal cortex and amygdala.

sources.title: Neuroscience of Human Social Interactions and Adult Attachment Style
sources.key_findings: Synthesized human neuroimaging evidence showing that avoidant attachment involves prefrontal suppression of outward social approach cues alongside persistent amygdala threat responses during social exclusion or stress.

sources.title: Adult Attachment Representations, Parental Responsiveness, and Infant Attachment: A Meta-Analysis on the Predictive Validity of the Adult Attachment Interview
sources.key_findings: Meta-analyzed Strange Situation distributions across samples (~65-70% secure, ~20% avoidant, ~10-15% ambivalent/resistant) and linked caregiver sensitivity to infant secure-base regulation.

sources.title: Social Regulation of the Cortisol Levels in Early Human Development
sources.key_findings: Critically evaluated HPA-axis cortisol buffering across infant laboratory paradigms, emphasizing how responsive caregiving prevents cortisol elevation even when behavioral crying occurs, while highlighting temperament and contextual moderators.
